title.narrative: Output 1.4. Strengthened social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative:
National and local Economic and Social Councils (ESCs) undertook to meet at least once a month. The ESC has been consulted on the second and fourht packages of COVID-19 relief measures to support the economy and the citizens at risk of poverty, prior to their adoption by the Government. new work arrangements (teleworking, OSH) and labour relations reform. With the support of the European Union, the ILO provided training to the members of the standing committees of the Economic and Social Council (ESC) on two selected topics: (1) the assessment of the key labour market and poverty indicators using the ILO's forecasting model, and (2) collective bargaining, with particular focus on wage setting. Customized training programme was delivered on Sustainable Development Goals and the EU Acquis Priorities.
The ILO, upon the request of the ESC, developed a legal analysis on regulation and implementation of Telework, including Guidelines on the implementation of the European Framework Agreement on Telework. The report will feed the process of drafting the new Labour Relations Law, in particular, the provisions regulating the alternative modes of work arrangement.
The ILO assisted the development of a communication strategy of the ESC and the launch of two campaigns implemented by the ESCs in coordination with the LESCs.
The ILO developed a technical note on extension of legal and social protection to temporary workers dismissed during the pandemic.
The ILO provided technical and logistical support to the national ESC specialised standing committee to negotiate and reach a tripartite agreement over a new draft Labour Relations Act.

description.narrative: The diagnostic Study on nonstandard forms of employment was validated in a tripartite meeting on 22 December 2021. The diagnosis will encompass the diverse forms of employment that are either regulated or in use in North Macedonia, in particular temporary employment, part-time work, contractual arrangements involving multiple parties, disguised employment and dependent self-employment. With the support of the European Union, the ILO developed a legal study on selected non-standard forms of employment, namely fixed-term contracts and disguised employment relationships, and a separate study on the regulation and implementation of "telework" in North Macedonian. These studies were published and served as building blocks for the preparation of the national diagnosis. With the support of Sweden, the ILO is carrying out a national diagnosis of diverse forms of work arrangements, including policy recommendations for ensuring effective labour and social protection for the workers concerned, and will facilitate its tripartite validation. In addition to the above study, the diagnosis is prepared on the basis of a legal study of the diverse forms of employment that are either regulated on in use in North Macedonia, an economic study using statistical data available from the Labour Force Survey, as well as a survey of workers and employers concerned by diverse forms of employment. This will constitute a solid ground for the preparation of policy recommendations, which will be submitted to the government for its validation in consultation with social partners.
